'''''Jianghanichthys''''' is an extinct genus of freshwater [[Cypriniformes|cypriniform]] fish from the [[Thanetian|Late Paleocene]] to [[Ypresian|Early Eocene]] of central and southern China, and the only member of the family '''Jianghanichthyidae'''.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last1=Liu |first1=Juan |last2=Chang |first2=Mee-Mann |last3=Wilson |first3=Mark V. H. |last4=Murray |first4=Alison M. |date=2015-11-02 |title=A new family of Cypriniformes (Teleostei, Ostariophysi) based on a redescription of † Jianghanichthys hubeiensis (Lei, 1977) from the Eocene Yangxi Formation of China |url=http://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/02724634.2015.1004073 |journal=Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology |language=en |volume=35 |issue=6 |article-number=e1004073 |doi=10.1080/02724634.2015.1004073 |bibcode=2015JVPal..35E4073L |issn=0272-4634|url-access=subscription }}</ref> It is the oldest cypriniform fish known from body fossils, and the most [[Basal (phylogenetics)|basal]] known cypriniform.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Near |first1=Thomas J. |last2=Thacker |first2=Christine E. |date=2024-04-18 |title=Phylogenetic Classification of Living and Fossil Ray-Finned Fishes (Actinopterygii) |journal=Bulletin of the Peabody Museum of Natural History |volume=65 |issue=1 |page=101 |doi=10.3374/014.065.0101 |bibcode=2024BPMNH..65..101N |issn=0079-032X|doi-access=free }}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite journal |last1=Liu |first1=Juan |last2=Chang |first2=Meemann |last3=Zhang |first3=Jiangyong |last4=Chen |first4=Gengjiao |last5=Shi |first5=Chaofan |date=2024-05-09 |title=Taxonomic revision and type specimens' location of jianghanichthyids (Ostariophysii: Cypriniformes) from Buxin Formation, Sanshui Basin, China |journal=Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology |volume=43 |issue=6 |article-number=e2342857 |language=en |doi=10.1080/02724634.2024.2342857 |issn=0272-4634|doi-access=free }}</ref> 

The genus name ''Jianghanichthys'' derives from "[[Jianghan Plain|Jianghan]]", the place where the first fossil remains of ''J. hubeiensis'' were found, and "ichthys" derives from the Greek word for 'fish'.<ref name=":0" /> It is also known as the "'''Chan Han fish'''" in the fossil trade.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bob Gillham collection {{!}} Earth Sciences Museum |url=https://uwaterloo.ca/earth-sciences-museum/supporters/donated-collections/bob-gillham-collection |access-date=2024-01-22 |website=uwaterloo.ca |language=en}}</ref> 

==Taxonomy==
Three species are known, two of which were previously placed in ''[[Osteochilus]]:''

* '''''{{extinct}}J. huachongensis''''' <small>Liu & Zhang, 2026</small> - middle-late Eocene of [[Guangdong]], China ([[Huachong Formation]])<ref name=":2">{{Cite journal |last=Liu |first=Juan |last2=Zhang |first2=Jiang-Yong |date=2026 |title=New Eocene jianghanichthyid (Teleostei: Cypriniformes) from the Huachong Formation with description of its cephalic sensory canals |url=https://cdnsciencepub.com/doi/10.1139/cjz-2025-0098 |journal=Canadian Journal of Zoology |volume=104 |pages=1–11 |doi=10.1139/cjz-2025-0098 |issn=0008-4301|hdl=1807/154064 |hdl-access=free }}</ref>
* {{extinct}}'''''J. hubeiensis''''' <small>(Lei, 1977)</small> ([[type species]]) - Early Eocene ([[Ypresian]]) of [[Hubei]], China ([[Yangxi Formation]])<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Yangxi Formation |url=https://chinalex.geolex.org/formations/Yangxi%20Fm |access-date=2024-07-27 |website=chinalex.geolex.org}}</ref>
* {{extinct}}'''''J. sanshuiensis''''' <small>(Li & Wang, 1979)</small> - Late Paleocene ([[Thanetian]]) and Ypresian of Guangdong, China ([[Buxin Formation]]) (=''Osteochilus laticorpus'' <small>Li & Wang, 1979</small>, ''O. longipinnatus'' <small>Li & Wang, 1979</small>)<ref name=":1" />

There are still disagreements as to the scientific classification, name and age of this genus. However the body shape of ''Jianghanichthys ''differs from that of all ''[[Amyzon (fish)|Amyzon]]'' species. ''J. hubeiensis'' was reclassified from ''Osteochilus'' into the new genus ''Jianghanichthys'' in 1987, and in 2015 it was moved from the [[Catostomidae]] to the new, basal family Jianghanichthyidae.<ref name=":0" /> In 2024, the slightly older species ''J. sanshuiensis'' was also reclassified into this genus from ''Osteochilus'', marking both a slight temporal extension and a range extension for the genus.<ref name=":1" /> A new slightly younger species, ''J. huachongensis'', was described in 2026. Specimens of ''J. huachongensis'', are known to have exceptionally well-preserved sensory canals that differ from those of other species in the genus, suggesting that there was a much greater degree of morphological diversity within early-diverging cypriniform clades.<ref name=":2" />

==Distribution==
[[File:Amyzon hunanensis 01.jpg|left|thumb|Fossil of ''J. hubeiensis'']]
These fishes lived in the early [[Paleogene]] period. Fossils of ''Jianghanichthys'' have been found in [[Hubei]] and [[Guangdong]], [[China]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /> 

Fossils of ''J. hubeiensis'' are quite common and can be found in most shops.{{Where|date=August 2020}} Most of these are among the thousands of well-preserved ''J. hubeiensis'' fossils which were discovered in an outcrop in a farm near [[Songzi]] in the 1980s. However, overcollection by commercial fossil collectors had destroyed this locality by 2005, though some new specimens have since been discovered with later fieldwork.<ref name=":0" />
